readerTitle: Quibi had $1.75 billion. It still skipped the cheapest test.
caseNote: 실제 기업 (Quibi, 2020년 출시·종료) + 가상 적용 (접이식 물류 상자 제조사)
insight: 돈으로 살 수 있는 것은 규모이지 증거가 아니다. 자금이 많을수록 작게 시험하는 데 더 큰 절제가 필요하다.
misconception: 충분한 자금과 뛰어난 인재, 큰 마케팅이 있으면 검증 단계를 건너뛰고 바로 크게 시작해도 된다.

sources.text: Jeffrey Katzenberg & Meg Whitman, open letter announcing Quibi's shutdown (October 21, 2020), published on Medium
Quibi launch announcements and coverage, April 2020 (pricing $4.99 with ads / $7.99 without, 90-day free trial, mobile-only short episodes)
News coverage of Quibi's funding (about $1.75 billion raised) and shutdown, e.g. The Wall Street Journal, The Verge, Variety (2020)
Roku press release on acquiring Quibi's content library (January 2021)

factChecks.note: 투자 유치 금액 약 17.5억 달러는 여러 언론에 보도된 수치입니다. 카드에는 "a reported $1.75 billion"으로 적었습니다. 게시 전 1차 보도로 다시 확인하세요.
출시일 2020년 4월 6일, 요금(광고 포함 $4.99, 광고 없음 $7.99), 90일 무료 체험, 에피소드 10분 이하 형식을 출시 당시 보도로 확인하세요.
2020년 슈퍼볼 광고 집행 여부와, 출시 후 다운로드가 둔화됐다는 앱 분석 업체 인용 보도를 확인하세요. 구체적 수치는 일부러 넣지 않았습니다.
종료 발표일 2020년 10월 21일과 공개 서한 인용문 "because the idea itself wasn't strong enough to justify a stand-alone streaming service or because of our timing"의 정확한 문구를 원문으로 확인하세요.
출시 초기 클립 공유·스크린샷이 어려웠다는 리뷰 지적, Roku의 콘텐츠 인수(2021년 1월)를 확인하세요.
2번 카드의 선택지는 실제 Quibi 경영진이 검토한 대안이 아니라 판단 연습용으로 구성한 것입니다. 내부 의사결정 내용은 지어내지 않았습니다.

cards.title: Quibi had $1.75 billion. It lasted about six months.
body: In 2020, Quibi launched with famous founders, Hollywood stars and a reported $1.75 billion from investors. It was built for phones: shows cut into episodes of 10 minutes or less.
About six months later, it announced it was shutting down. The money wasn't the problem. What the money let it skip was.

image.label: A giant stage built for a crowd, with only a few people watching
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 거대한 스마트폰 모양의 무대와 수천 개의 빈 객석, 앞줄에만 관객 몇 명. 무대 뒤에 돈 자루가 높이 쌓여 있음. 실제 Quibi 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: You have the money. How do you launch?
body: It's 2019. You run a new streaming service of short shows made for phones. No one has proven people will pay for this format.
You've raised well over a billion dollars, and star creators are signing on. What do you do?

options.text: Launch nationwide with a full slate of shows and a big ad campaign
options.feedback: You'd reach millions fast and look like the leader. But you'd spend most of the money before learning whether people keep watching after the free trial.

options.text: Launch to a small group first and track who keeps watching and paying
options.feedback: You give up a splashy debut and some secrecy. In return you learn the one thing money can't tell you: whether people come back.

options.text: Wait a year and make even more shows before launching
options.feedback: More content might help, but it adds cost without answering the core question. Waiting isn't the same as testing.

cards.title: Quibi went big on day one.
body: Quibi launched across the US on April 6, 2020. It had a large library of original shows, a Super Bowl ad, prices of $4.99 a month with ads or $7.99 without, and a 90-day free trial.
News reports citing app-tracking firms said downloads slowed soon after launch. On October 21, 2020, the founders announced the shutdown. Its shows were later sold to Roku.

image.label: Timeline from launch in April to shutdown in October 2020
image.brief: 가로 타임라인 인포그래픽. 왼쪽 "Apr 2020 · Launch"에 큰 폭죽, 가운데 "Free trial ends"에서 선이 꺾여 내려감, 오른쪽 "Oct 2020 · Shutdown". 구체적 사용자 수치는 표시하지 않음. 로고 없음.

cards.title: Scaling before proof
body: **Premature scaling** means spending to grow before you know customers will stay.
Quibi built for millions from the start: content, marketing and a large team. The proof it needed was much smaller. Would a few thousand people keep watching, and pay, once the trial ended?
That answer was cheap to get. Quibi bought the scale first and got the answer last.

cards.title: Even the founders weren't sure why.
body: In their shutdown letter, Jeffrey Katzenberg and Meg Whitman said Quibi was failing "because the idea itself wasn't strong enough to justify a stand-alone streaming service or because of our timing."
Timing did hurt. Quibi was built for commutes and waiting rooms, and in 2020 people were stuck at home. Early reviews also noted it was hard to share clips on social media.
But a small test would have shown which problems mattered, at a fraction of the cost.

cards.eyebrow: A new way to see it
cards.title: Big money removes the pressure to test.
body: A small startup has to test. It can't afford a large mistake, so it learns step by step.
Quibi could afford to skip that step. It could pay for top talent, a national launch and huge ads all at once. **Money buys scale. It doesn't buy proof.**
The bigger the budget, the more discipline it takes to start small.

image.label: A coin buying a megaphone but not a magnifying glass
image.brief: 두 칸 일러스트. 왼쪽: 돈 자루로 대형 확성기·광고판을 사는 장면("Scale"). 오른쪽: 돈 자루를 내밀어도 닫혀 있는 돋보기 상자, 옆에 작은 실험용 비커와 몇 명의 고객("Proof"). 로고 없음.

cards.title: Starting small isn't always right.
body: Some businesses only work at scale. A marketplace with too few sellers can look like a failure in a small test, even when the idea is sound.
A test can also mislead if the test group doesn't look like your real customers.
And we can't rerun 2020. No one knows whether Quibi would have survived in a normal year. The lesson isn't that Quibi was doomed. It's that it learned the answer at the most expensive moment.

cards.title: Now it's a factory.
body: You've designed a reusable shipping crate that folds flat. Three pilot customers like the samples.
An investor offers enough money to build a full production line for 100,000 crates a year. What do you do?

options.text: Build the full line now, before a competitor does
options.feedback: You'd be ready for big demand, but you'd lock in large fixed costs before knowing whether customers reorder.

options.text: Make a few thousand with a contract manufacturer and track reorders
options.feedback: Each crate costs more and growth is slower. But reorders show whether demand is real before you commit the big money.

options.text: Build the line, but at half the size
options.feedback: Less risky than the full line, yet still a big bet on demand you haven't seen. Half a guess is still a guess.

cards.title: Money buys scale, not proof.
body: Before spending to grow, find the smallest test that shows customers stay and pay again.
**Try it today:** pick the biggest spending plan on your desk. Write down the one thing it assumes about customers, and the cheapest way to check it first.
